_comment_family: The third static cut of Montserrat in this folder, and the lightest
of them. montserrat-bold.json is the note to read first: it is where
the argument for declaring a full name rather than 'Montserrat' is
made, and it holds for all three packs.
A SemiBold is not one of the four styles the old family model has
room for, so the static build gives it a family of its own exactly
the way it does the ExtraBold: name ID 1 here reads 'Montserrat
SemiBold' with 'Regular' as the subfamily, and the real family shows
up only in the typographic names (16/17) as 'Montserrat' +
'SemiBold'. Declaring the full name is therefore not a workaround on
this pack - it is the file's own family name.
Three cuts of one family in one folder is also the reason none of
them may answer to the family name: fontguard keys its check by
family, so each cut has to be verified in its own right rather than
_comment_weight: 600, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. It matters here for the reason it matters on the Bold beside
it: the face this pack is paired with on rap-lore is that Bold, and
the 100 units between 600 and 700 ARE that channel's highlight. A
block asked for at the wrong weight would not look wrong on its own -
it would quietly close the one gap the highlight is made of, or
invite a browser to synthesise a difference the metrics do not know
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the Windows full name (name ID 4) and the second the
PostScript name; both name this one cut rather than the family, so a
machine answering to either is answering with the SemiBold.
'Montserrat' on its own is absent here for the reason it is absent on
the other two, and the consequence has a particular shape on the
lightest cut of the three: a block that fell back to the family would
come out in whatever weight the machine keeps as Montserrat's
default, which on most machines is the Regular - lighter than what
was asked for, which on a caption over a photograph is the direction
that costs legibility rather than merely looking wrong.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and they are the
Bold's entries reached at a different weight, for the reason the
ExtraBold's are: the difference between block and highlight on the
channel set in this pair is a WEIGHT, and weight travels in the font
string beside the family rather than inside it (see textProps in
js/text.js). Sharing every fallback is therefore what keeps the two
one step apart wherever the substitute family has the cuts.
No Impact and no Arial Black, which most of this folder falls through
and which would be wrong here twice over. Montserrat is a geometric
text sans at 600, not a heavy display cut, so a condensed grotesque
behind it is the furthest thing the machine could offer from what
went missing.
Segoe UI is on every Windows this app runs on and Arial is the floor.
Neither has a real SemiBold, so 600 lands on their Regular or their
Bold depending on the machine - and where it lands on the Bold, the
step this channel's highlight is made of closes. That is the ordinary
cost of a face that never arrived, and it is reported rather than
drawn.
